item.text:
**1B.2 Research Note: Abiy Ahmed in 2024**

**Interpretation:** I found no reliable 2024 evidence that Abiy Ahmed used nuclear-specific rhetoric at all, let alone recklessly. The usable 2024 record is indirect: it shows repeated peace-forward language on Somalia, Egypt, the Nile, and internal conflict, plus one fact-check debunking a viral “stern warning” clip. Because Ethiopia is not a nuclear-armed state, the lens is only informatively assessable through broader security rhetoric.

| Date | Title | Publisher | Recoverable page URL | Claim-level summary | QIDs |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2024-02-06 | Ethiopia's leader plays down fears of conflict with Somalia over a planned naval port | Associated Press via CityNews | https://kitchener.citynews.ca/2024/02/06/ethiopias-leader-plays-down-fears-of-conflict-with-somalia-over-a-planned-naval-port/ | Abiy said he had “no intention” of going to war with Somalia, framed peace with Somalia as mutually beneficial, and also tried to reassure Egypt on the Nile dam issue. This is the clearest 2024 evidence of restrained, non-brinkmanship security rhetoric. | 1B.2, 1B.1 |
| 2024-09-04 | Ethiopian leader’s speech did not include ‘stern warning’ to Somalia and Egypt | AFP Fact Check | https://factcheck.afp.com/doc.afp.com.36FG9HB | AFP’s fact check found that a viral video claiming Abiy issued a “stern warning” to Somalia and Egypt was misleading; the underlying footage was from an older Tigray-related speech and did not mention Somalia or Egypt. This undercuts a claim of reckless 2024 warning language. | 1B.2 |
| 2024-10-13 | PM Abiy Says CFA’s Entry into Force Ensures Utilization of Shared Water Resources to Benefit All | ENA English | https://www.ena.et/web/eng/w/eng_5283840 | Abiy described the Nile Basin framework as a cooperative milestone that would ensure shared water resources “benefit all” and called on non-signatories to join regional cooperation. This is consistent with careful, de-escalatory rhetoric on a major security-sensitive issue. | 1B.2, 1B.1 |
| 2024-10-31 | Abiy Reaffirms Government’s Commitment for Durable Peace, Security | ENA English | https://www.ena.et/web/eng/w/eng_5380692 | Abiy said the government “always opts for peace over forceful approach,” prioritized peaceful resolution of conflicts, and urged dialogue and forgiveness rather than force. This is strong evidence of responsible rhetoric on security and conflict. | 1B.2, 1B.1 |
| 2024-10-31 | Ethiopia Pursues Peaceful Access to Red Sea Amid Growing Economy: PM Abiy | ENA English | https://www.ena.et/web/eng/w/eng_5380659 | Abiy said Ethiopia sought Red Sea access “in a peaceful manner,” that the agenda was “not about confrontation,” and that the goal was mutual benefit and economic growth. This is relevant because it directly rejects escalatory framing in a high-tension regional dispute. | 1B.2, 1B.1 |

**Search gap**

- I searched directly for 2024 nuclear-related phrasing around Abiy Ahmed, Ethiopia, Somalia, Egypt, war, and rhetoric.
- I found no reliable 2024 source showing Abiy threatening nuclear use, normalizing nuclear weapons, or using apocalyptic nuclear language.
- The only nuclear-adjacent material in the 2024 record was about peaceful development, but the usable sources I found were not actually nuclear-specific enough to support an accepted claim for this lens.

**Bottom line**

- On this lens, the evidence is overwhelmingly on the responsible side.
- There is no solid 2024 evidence of reckless nuclear rhetoric.
- The strongest support for a positive judgment is Abiy’s repeated public framing of disputes as matters for peace, cooperation, and mutual benefit, especially in the Somalia, Nile, and Red Sea contexts.
